card.band: 8 h. A frontier agent covers the common functions but misses coercion rules, array behaviour, and financial iterative solvers (IRR, XIRR, RATE). A weaker model implements only the simple ones. Buckets by category.
card.cheat: Hard-coding results is not possible because the hidden formulas and arguments differ. The original sources are removed from the snapshot and from the node_modules.
card.grading: Vitest-style hidden cases: formula in, value or error out, including array broadcasting and error propagation. Upstream function tests are the base, extended by cases cross-checked against a spreadsheet reference. Compare with numeric tolerance 1e-9 and exact error codes. Visible samples ship; the hidden count is not found.
card.reference: The deleted upstream function files (several thousand lines of TS). They score 1 on upstream-derived cases.
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot of the engine-formula package with the function implementations for the financial, statistical, date/time, text, lookup and engineering categories deleted. The agent rebuilds them behind the existing function registry, with Excel error and coercion semantics, and the build passes with pnpm.

source_notes: SWE-smith profile (typescript): its suite runs in a container; test command: pnpm test -- --passWithNoTests --reporter=verbose. The repo is used by a SWE-bench-family dataset.

v1.kill_reason: As written (six categories, about 55 financial function folders alone, exact 1e-9 and Excel error codes), no frontier trial is likely to reach 0.9 of the reference within 8 h or even 20 h (frontier_hours about 60). Salvage: re-seed with two or three categories (for example text, lookup and date, or the non-iterative financial functions) on the 8 h tier. Also unverified: smoke_build was empty (not run), and node_modules may leak compiled function code (K11 risk).

Band.why: Frontier coverage of common functions is plausible but there is no dated public evidence, so the cap is 3

Build.why: Roughly 3-5 days to stripping, cross-check set and leak audit

Fit.why: TS/pnpm fits the CPU sandbox, but the build and test runtime are unmeasured

Hor.why: Many modules and categories give sustained work, but the 8 h tier is too short for the whole scope

Lic.why: Apache-2.0 permits shipping the snapshot and reference

Multi.why: Per-category and per-function buckets give steady partial credit

Nov.why: Neighbours are 0.26-0.30 (sibling seeds, unverified) and the SpreadsheetBench family is related but a different deliverable

Real.why: Public Apache-2.0 repo at a pinned commit with 22.7k stars; the function directories and irr/xirr/rate folders exist

Ref.why: The deleted upstream files are a complete permissive implementation; their hidden-case score is unverified

Seal.why: Upstream is public and formulajs is recallable in outline; the snapshot closes repo access, but the node_modules dist leak is unchecked

Surf.why: Upstream tests plus cross-checked cases could reach thousands, but the hidden count is not found and the per-function upstream test files are not visible

spike_plan.kill_if: node_modules leaks compiled function implementations (K11); the build cannot run offline; or even the narrowed scope needs more than 20 h.
spike_plan.pass_if: Offline build green; the deleted-start fails all category cases; node_modules contains no Excel-function code; a narrowed scope of two or three categories looks finishable in 8 h.
steps: In a throwaway container with network, clone univer at 1e58578 and run pnpm install and the engine-formula build; record whether it is green offline and how long it takes (smoke_build is empty, so this is the first real check).

Search node_modules for compiled copies of the target functions: grep for IRR/XIRR/RATE/VLOOKUP in @univerjs dist bundles and for formulajs, jstat or numeric packages. Any hit is a seal leak, so kill or strip it.
Copy the repo, delete the six category folders, and run the upstream function tests; confirm the deleted-start scores 0 on those cases and count the per-test results.
Count the upstream per-function test cases that exist for financial, text, lookup and date, to size the visible base.

Use formulajs in the spike container only (never in the image) to produce IRR, XIRR and RATE values on about 30 sampled inputs and compare them with the upstream outputs at 1e-9. This shows how far a recall-based agent gets.
Decide the scope: if the whole scope exceeds 20 h, re-seed with two or three categories (for example text, lookup and date) on the 8 h tier.

v1.summary: Univer @ 1e58578 is real, Apache-2.0, and its financial, text, lookup, date and engineering function folders exist, so the paper trail holds. The seed as written is too big for any frontier trial to reach 0.9 of the reference in 8 h, so I kill it as K9 and suggest a narrower two-to-three-category scope, after the node_modules leak check and build probe (not yet run) pass.
